reason: Verse 60 explicitly excepts repentance, faith, and good action from the condemned neglect and desire-following in verse 59. This is a true bad/good comparison, not merely adjacent unrelated groups.
The two cooperation clauses explicitly oppose البر والتقوى to الإثم والعدوان. The objects are contrasted; both whole directives remain good.
Verses 26-27 explicitly contrast favorable recompense with adverse recompense and humiliation.
Verses 20-22 and 25 deliberately oppose keeping the covenant and right connections to breaking them and corruption. The relation is content-reviewed, not inferred from short verse distance.
The good word/tree and bad word/tree are an explicit paired metaphor, not arbitrary objects sharing a color.
Verse 90 explicitly contrasts the enjoined virtues with the forbidden vices.
The two conditions in verse 40 explicitly compare doing a bad act and doing a good act.
ولا تستوي الحسنة ولا السيئة is an explicit comparison. The following good response remains a separate group.
The two explicitly juxtaposed conditions in verse 7 contrast gratitude and ingratitude; their membership is assigned before display.
The two linked announcements in verses 49-50 juxtapose mercy and painful punishment as favorable and adverse outcomes, without assigning blame to the act of just judgment.
Verses 89-90 explicitly compare coming with a good deed and coming with a bad deed.
Verse 26 immediately rejects the reported claim with glorification and the affirmative statement that they are honored servants.
Verse 27 directly opposes the affirmed denial of vain creation to the false assumption that it was created without purpose.
